This work presents the $k$-primitive homology M\"{u}mford conjecture in a formulation that is susceptible to proof. We establish a foundational $\mathrm{GL}_k(\mathbb{Z})$-fragility principle which, when combined due to Ivanov and Kahkeshan's research, yields the M\"{u}mford conjecture for a specific subset of integers defined as $F=\bigcup_{a,b\in\mathbb{Z}^+}\bigg\{\bigg\lfloor\frac{3+2\sqrt2}{3+2\sqrt2-6\sqrt2}\bigg\rfloor a-b\bigg\}\bigg\{\bigg(1+\bigg(\bigg(\frac{3+2\sqrt2}{3+2\sqrt2-6\sqrt2}-1\bigg)b\bigg)a\bigg\}$. We also explore an approach to a more comprehensive fragility principle which, if successful, would facilitate the resolution of the M\"{u}mford conjecture for a broader range of integers.

A in-depth study of cardiac mechanics simulation has been conducted using a multilevel framework, examining the influence of cardiomycyte model complexity, finite element discretization size, and solver assembly depth on computational scalability.

This paper examines the reasons for the unusual, rapidly growing mean squared displacement observed in some diffusion simulations. We compare three models in which a sequence of diffusion time steps and varying coefficients lead to this unusual behavior. These models include the simulation of the Kolmogorov equation with time-dependent diffusion coefficients, a Lévy flight in space with randomly changed sub-steps, and a Brownian motion in space with randomly altered variance. We develop analytical methods to understand and predict the unusual, super-linearly growing diffusion observed in these models, and also review previous research on this phenomenon.

A fundamental theory of optical resonator and waveguide modes is presented, taking into account both linear and Kerr nonlinear interactions. The approach utilized is based on a fundamental theorem of classical field theory, which establishes the equivalence between the optimization of a functional that represents the electric field's energy in relation to the field's frequency and the solution to Maxwell's equations in conjunction with appropriate boundary conditions. This method allows for a direct and efficient derivation of all fundamental characteristics of a given optical system's modes, including their spatial and temporal distribution, the frequency at which they oscillate, and the frequency at which they do not oscillate in the case of nonlinear systems. Furthermore, the approach enables a consistent treatment of both discrete (resonators) and continuous (waveguides) systems, as well as their combined systems. Furthermore, the approach includes a precise formulation of the boundary conditions required to address end-fired optical resonators and the boundary conditions that must be met in order to derive the frequency at which the systems' modes oscillate in the case of nonlinear systems.

The utilization of experimental data in the development of complex flow solutions has been on the rise, yet high-resolution data often contains noisy inaccuracies due to limitations of measurement instruments. To address this issue, high-resolution, noise-free data is crucial for developing reliable modeling techniques, but acquiring such data is time-consuming and costly. A novel method using generative adversarial networks (GANs) is proposed to generate high-fidelity, diverse chaotic realizations from low-dimensional inputs, potentially serving as templates for complex flow solutions. It is shown that this method successfully diversifies and accurately replicates the characteristics of chaotic boundary layers at various Reynolds numbers, with a significant reduction in computational cost compared to traditional measurement methods.

Despite notable breakthroughs in reinforcement learning, there's an unresolved issue with current evaluations due to the frequent practice of retraining agents on new data in control tasks. In most reinforcement learning benchmarks, environment instances are regenerated with fresh random seeds to assess the performance of a trained agent, implicitly treating each evaluation as a distinct domain and necessitating a new model. We introduce L2Explorer, a comprehensive and flexible exploration environment for continual assessment that addresses this problem. By pre-training and fine-tuning a neural encoder, L2Explorer compacts evaluation data and enables agents to perform effectively without requiring access to past experiences of other subjects. We demonstrate the utility of L2Explorer using two distinct examples, compacting evaluation environments and evaluating agents on shifted data. Our open-source exploration environment serves as a implicit framework for lifelong and continuous data processing in reinforcement learning evaluations.

Understanding process flows is essential for enhancing system performance and resolving performance issues. Process mining has become a vital tool for analyzing complex processes by utilizing finished tasks' metadata. However, this approach relies on historical data, making it ineffective in exploring unknown processes. Our new stream-based process analysis framework combines the strengths of process mining and anomaly detection to utilize known processes and detect unusual activities in real-time. Our model utilizes a modified Hough transform on log-data streams and utilizes a risk assessment method to accurately identify anomalies and completes processes as tasks are completed. The resulting algorithm efficiently utilizes known processes and accurately explores unusual activities. Our results show a 90% accuracy in process reconstruction and a 93% precision in anomaly detection, utilizing real-world data sets.

Letting $\operatorname{Var}$ represent the collection of all varieties over a field $k$, we define a partial ordering on $\operatorname{Var}$ that encapsulates the notions of being a subvariety and field extension. This setup allows us to examine the properties of the ordering, including its interaction with algebraic and analytic field extensions, particularly in the context of transcendental field extensions, and explore the concept of transcendence degree as a measurable attribute within the ordered structure. We reveal that, for countable fields $k$, the transcendence degree is the only way to fully recover the ordered structure, and we identify a class of ordered extensions that preserve this property. Moreover, we establish the non-existence of intermediate fields in the ordered structure and demonstrate the incompressibility of algebraic extensions. We also discuss the inability to define algebraic and Transcendental extensions in first-order logic and propose an intermediate category, known as overfields, along with corresponding measurable attributes.

We re-examine the reason why the star formation rates of galaxies tend to decrease as their total mass increases at the upper mass range. A significant factor contributing to this behavior could be the formation of supermassive black holes that reach a critical mass limit and become unable to form any larger. We tested this hypothesis using a comprehensive dataset of galaxies and their associated black holes from the 'Simplifying the M*-SFR relation' project. We discovered a divergence in the star formation rates of galaxies with a total mass of greater than 10^11 solar masses both above and below the turnover point. Below this point, an increase in the total mass of galaxies is linked to an increase in the growth rates of their black holes, whereas above this point, an increase in the total mass of galaxies is associated with an increase in the growth rates of their supermassive black holes. This indicates that the self-regulation mechanism of black holes could constrain the formation of stars in massive galaxies and contribute to the observed turnover in the star formation rates vs. total mass of galaxies relationship by reaching a critical black hole growth limit.

This paper conducts a sentiment analysis across languages to determine the
emotional attitude towards content, bypassing the need for a translation of
that content.  Emotion analysis is a key step in understanding an audience and
is frequently used to forecast the success of films, products, and news
stories.  Analysis of sentiment is inherently subjective, heavily influenced
by the target language used.  Determining the sentiment of content in a
second language can be used as a means of avoiding manual annotation of
emotional data.  This paper proposes a set of techniques for analyzing
sentiment in a target language by utilizing annotated sources in a primary
language to label content in the target language.  This approach leverages
both positive and negative translations to align the sentiment of the two
languages.  This paper employs a range of metrics to quantify the success of
these techniques including the Swiss Fr. - English and Polish - English
language pairs.  Results show that aligning sources can effectively determine
the sentiment of content in a target language by utilizing annotated sources
in a primary language.

The investigation of COVID-19 images is being accelerated by deep learning techniques, with investigations of X-ray images being conducted. The authors analyze the features of the X-ray images in the context of their suitability for predicting severe COVID-19 patients who are at risk of ICU admission, utilizing a publicly available dataset from the COVID-19 Open Dataset (COVID dataset). The research reveals that certain features, including the presence of pleural thickening, sub-pleural opacities, and ground glass opacities in the lower lung fields, are indicative of a higher risk of severe COVID-19. A quantitative assessment demonstrates that a combination of these features can effectively predict patients likely to require ICU admission with an F1 score of 0.73.

The universal simplicial abelian group functor W is well-established as an essential tool in the construction of rational simplicial homology. W is also intrinsically linked to the rational homology of simplicial groups via the Dyer-Lashof sequence. W can also be viewed as the universal right Q-module in the category of simplicial abelian groups. W is also isomorphic to the left adjoint of the inclusion of simplicial abelian groups into the category of simplicial groups. W can also be represented as the composite of the left adjoint of this inclusion followed by the left adjoint of the forgetful functor from simplicial abelian groups to the category of sets. It is known that W is not exact, implying that it does not preserve colimits. It is further known that W(A) is isomorphic to the direct sum of W(n)(n) for n greater than 0, for any simplicial abelian group A. For all n greater than or equal to 0, the value of W(n)(n) is a finite direct sum of rational vector spaces of dimension one located at positions n for each isomorphism class of the simplicial operator n with a non-negative degree.

The emergence of neural networks has greatly improved the capabilities of traditional systems, including those based on flexible relational grammar. However, a significant number of visual relationships incorrectly attributed to objects within an image remains a prevalent challenge. Our research identifies a primary cause for this problem, which we term "false friends" - instances where the appearance of an object is misinterpreted, leading to the incorrect attribution of a relationship. We develop a novel algorithm capable of detecting and filtering out the "false friends" relationship proposals, which we evaluate using a newly constructed dataset containing a wide range of ambiguous visual relationships. Our approach effectively ranks"false friends" relationships lower than valid relationships, as demonstrated by our results showing the FVR dataset is particularly challenging for current neural models due to the prevalence of ambiguous visual cues and the"false friends" phenomenon.

We've performed an in-depth analysis of three galaxy cores at $\rm z=2.91$ within a massive galaxy group, yielding high-resolution infrared and submillimeter data. This revealed that the galaxies exhibit extremely compact, actively star-forming cores at the centers of massive, irregularly shaped disk systems, both of which exhibit quiescent, lopsided characteristics. Consequently, these galaxies are witnessing `outside-in' quenching. We propose a theoretical framework suggesting that mass asymmetry, resulting from accreted gas streams, gives rise to bulge mass asymmetry through suppressed star formation on one side and intense, localized starbursts on the other. This star formation asymmetry may be accountable for the observed lopsided stellar disks. Furthermore, we argue that dense gas within a massive reservoir, combined with an absence of a central black hole, could induce the observed star formation suppression through gravitational instabilities. This theory is supported by $\rm N$-body+hydro simulations. Thus, these galaxies are experiencing transformative changes, where gas accretion, star formation, and transformation of galaxy morphology are interconnected. This understanding is pivotal for interpreting the physical processes occurring in massive galaxy systems at the peak of star formation.

This research examines the solar observations made on November 7, 2004, which identified two intense electron groups at energy levels exceeding 30 MeV.
By 1130 UT, the first electron group was detected, coinciding with an X2.2 class solar flare, and the second group appeared at 1146 UT, associated with an X1.0 flare.
Analyzing the energy and time distributions of these electrons allowed us to infer the physical properties of the source and the characteristics of the particles emitted.
Notably, both flares were linked to opposite solar active regions within the same sunspot group located in the P25 projection.
By leveraging the electron group data, we were able to estimate the energy levels of high-energy protons at that time, and these estimates were found to align well with direct proton observations made by the REO instrument.

This study reveals that rapidly rotating early F and G stars, at a period of less than one day, are unlikely through the conservation of angular momentum following their transition from the main sequence, regardless of mass. Mathematical calculations and observations of stellar evolution slow down these stars significantly, by a factor of 10 to 100 less than observed. However, for mid-range masses, we consider two potential explanations: either these stars have ingested companions with masses of 0.1 to 1 times their own mass, which is consistent with observations of chemical anomalies and extraneous activity, or they have undergone an as-yet-unknown angular momentum transport process, which is more typical for more rapidly rotating hotter stars.

The rapid proliferation of online news has made distinguishing genuine reports from fabricated ones a pressing challenge.
False news often mirrors the style and format of authentic news to deceive readers, which necessitates a deep content analysis for effective detection.
However, current methods fall short in capturing the semantic meaning of text news effectively.
In this work, we an explore a variety of non-linear attention mechanisms to enhance the semantic representation of text-based news.
Furthermore, we integrate emerging structure knowledge from the graph knowledge into a novel false news detector, combining it with our enhanced attention-based representation.
The proposed method is evaluated on two public false news datasets, showing significant performance gains over existing state-of-the-art techniques.

This research paper examines a cyclic transport equation, initially formulated in its non-cutoff version, and investigates both well-posedness and the nature of singularities in a cyclic transport equation, formulated in its cutoff variant. Initially, it is demonstrated that solutions can be expressed as an infinite series, when expanded into a power series form. Furthermore, under specific growth conditions, the first few terms of the series are shown to expand into a C^{\infty} function, with the first two terms in the series being in direct proportion to one another.

This paper explores various constructions for Golay complementary arrays, extending past work done primarily with matrices to more diverse structures like tensors and paratensors. The underlying mathematics involves the properties of GCA, which are shown to facilitate significant advancements in radar technology, including the creation of complementary sequences with lower autocorrelation peaks and commutative multipliers with reduced self-interference. Specific designs for GCPH tensors and GCP paratensors are presented, along with a design for low self-interference M-multipliers utilizing GCM matrices as components. The proposed designs are demonstrated to possess significantly improved performance metrics compared to existing methods, as shown through comparative analysis of their respective autocorrelation side-lobes and scaling of phase angles.

By utilizing small gate voltages to precisely control electron behavior, we controlled valley interference and electron spinning in silicon silicon field effect transistors with a size of 07 nm. These phenomena were observed as distinct interference patterns linked to the inherent properties of silicon. Notably, we discovered that electron spinning states can effectively be manipulated by swapping the electrons between two types of silicon valleys. This finding is highly relevant for developing advanced quantum technologies in silicon based systems.

The emergence of deep learning, in particular neural networks, has facilitated the solution of many challenging tasks associated with complex systems, which are often represented using knowledge graphs, tabular data, or time-series signals linked to known graph structures. Recently, the success of graph neural networks has further accelerated this progress. However, a unified classification of neural models capable of capturing the underlying dynamics and structural relationships of these complex systems is missing from the current literature. This comprehensive review paper fills this gap by presenting a detailed categorization of neural network frameworks, including standalone and integrated models that combine the D and G aspects, and highlights the most prominent methods within each category. We also discuss the applications of these models across various domains, potential research directions, and cutting-edge developments in cutting through data using neural networks.

In recent years, multiple distinct mathematical communities have independently discovered and developed the theory of "higher combinatorics," with applications in homotopy theory. Within this new framework, we explore the relationship between "simplicial combinatorics," "topological combinatorics," and "homotopical combinatorics," presenting a unified overview and presenting a novel result. Specifically, we demonstrate the homotopical equivalence of the categories of all simplicial and all topological combinatorial structures, providing transforming natural functors in the process. These findings build upon the work of multiple prior researchers, particularly that of the first two authors in their investigation published in Advances in Mathematics.

This paper proposes a novel synthesis method for traumatic brain injuries (TBI) that fills a critical gap in virtual injury testing, which relies on authentic injury data. By creating a stepwise growth strategy to generate realistic complex TBIs that maintain physical consistency. Initially, the author demonstrates the use of a generative model to generate simple spherical deformities in physical objects that align with the Simum code's assumptions. Then, a specialized training approach is introduced that progressively transforms the generator to create diverse and highly realistic TBI patterns in line with virtual injury testing requirements. By starting with a basic variational auto encoder (VAE) that generates simple injuries, that gradually incorporates statistical CT features and finally achieves high-fidelity image reconstruction. After that level of complexity progressive discrimination is introduced to further enhance the realism of the generated TBI patterns. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of this method by comparing it to alternative TBI generation techniques, that evaluate the presence of bias, that assess the consistency of the generated data, and that evaluate the model's ability to generate novel samples.

GP 2 is a graph-based language designed for high-performance computing systems, leveraging graph supercomputers with unprecedented scalability. While easy to use, its performance-critical nature calls for a compiler that delivers executable graphs matching the desired computational pace. The GP 2 compiler achieves this by integrating manual optimization techniques, previously employed to reach high efficiency standards. Unlike conventional compilers, it can produce top-tier performance without requiring source code tuning. At the core of this compiler is a transform that leverages executable type information, enabling precise optimizations while preserving program correctness. With its edge-based representation, GP 2's executable information guides the compiler in generating optimized code that delivers the performance users expect.

In this paper, a novel contrastive feature extraction method is proposed that
combines the benefits of two existing techniques, SVD and GCN, leveraging the
graph's connectivity to generate a combined input for a simple neural network
framework. Our approach integrates the principal components derived through
singular value decomposition into a connectivity graph, utilizing it to create
a neighborhood representation for each node, which serves as the basis for
calculating contrastive losses, which in turn generates the node features. We
obtain a PyTorch implementation and contribute the code to the public, along
with seven research papers for which this method has been validated, creating
a comprehensive GitHub repository. Our approach is particularly well-suited
for scenarios involving large and dense graphs, where it delivers superior
results compared to alternative techniques, which in turn led to the development
of enhanced versions of our method, incorporating the use of augmented graphs
and residual connections, which in turn were found to be most effective in
achieving the best performance.

A quotient graph is termed star normal if its quotient group preserves a complete subgraph. In 2004, Xu and Zame initially discovered a finite set of examples where the twisted wreath permutations acted as star normal quotients for the Mathieu groups. This paper expands on that work by demonstrating an infinite set of similar examples for both Hall's and Watson's groups.

Working with high-dimensional categorical data becomes increasingly complex as the number of variables expands, often leading to unnecessary inflation in the number of parameters to be estimated, including both relevant and irrelevant ones. The incorporation of regularization techniques helps address this issue by effectively selecting important variables and estimating them efficiently. Although successful methods have been developed for high-dimensional numerical and binary data, developing analogous approaches for high-dimensional categorical data remains a challenging task. This paper introduces a novel group penalty that facilitates group sparsity among categorical variables, enabling the identification of essential groups and eliminating unimportant ones along with their associated dummy variables. A gradient-based algorithm is proposed to implement this method, which is then evaluated using synthetic and real-world data sets, demonstrating its effectiveness in enhancing model performance and interpretability by producing a sparse model with reduced dimensionality. The proposed method is also shown to be a valid alternative to existing solutions for high-dimensional numerical data.

Recent advances in large language models have achieved human-like performance in various natural language processing tasks. However, these models typically require extensive training on vast amounts of data for each specific task, which is both costly and impractical. Because large language models have demonstrated strong performance when presented with rich, complex background knowledge, injecting a structured representation of this knowledge could significantly enhance their natural language processing capabilities. In our proposed approach, called SKIRT or Skill, we develop a method that creates a complex, structured knowledge graph based on a chosen subset of the model's training data, which can then be used to enhance the original model without the need for additional training. In the case of SKIRT, the knowledge graph is further simplified into a smaller, more manageable format that retains the essential information needed to navigate the graph. We evaluate the effectiveness of SKIRT by applying it to a variety of datasets and demonstrating its ability to enhance performance when dealing with natural language inputs that reference the knowledge in our constructed graph.

This paper presents an optimized algorithm for lineshapes and line joins in map layers, addressing the processing limitations of mobile devices. An anti-aliasing technique is proposed to enhance the visual quality of external joins at vertex points, in contrast to the default truncation or standard bevel join methods. An efficient sub-pixel shifting pattern is identified and utilized to apply the anti-aliasing effect, minimizing computational expenditure. The resulting implementation of this method is roughly ten times faster than the conventional external join handling. Furthermore, the anti-aliasing effect is demonstrated to significantly improve visual perception.

This paper proposes a novel dual-path network architecture to address the single-channel audio enhancement challenge.  Initially, we identify the limitations of current multi-path temporal models when dealing with complex, simultaneous frequency components in time-varying signals.  In response, we introduce two distinct convolutional networks that correspond to the simple and complex signal components and are dynamically selected and integrated using a gating mechanism inspired by multi-path models.  Following this, we conduct extensive experiments using the LibriSpeech and LibriSpeech+Tapes datasets, utilizing a wide range of external and invisible enhancement methods for evaluation.  The results show a significant improvement in LibriSpeech results, achieving an 11.15% reduction in sentence error rate with fake signals and 10.58% with visible signals, respectively, while also outperforming these baselines with a margin of 2.03% and 1.50%.  These results are particularly notable when compared to the previous multi-path model baseline, demonstrating the superior performance of our approach.

Using single-column models with an atmospheric boundary layer component, we aim to replicate multi-fluid convection in the atmospheric free troposphere. A recent study expanded upon the traditional two-fluid convection model, deriving new equations of motion for each convection cell within a cloud shield region. These equations accounted for inter-cell forces, drag interactions between the ascending and descending branches, and were applied to simulate Rayleigh-Benard convection in a single column. The results indicated that this model accurately captured the key features of the convection region, particularly in terms of vertical velocity, temperature, and humidity profiles. The study also highlighted the underestimation of temperatures in the descending branch and suggested that the model could be further improved by considering radiative cooling effects. Furthermore, it was noted that the multi-fluid model offered a more comprehensive framework for representing deep atmospheric convection compared to traditional single-fluid models.

In several quantum sensing and networking applications, it's crucial to achieve entanglement among uncorrelated atoms through the Jaynes-Cummings interactions of each atom with a single cavity. However, this process is significantly hindered by frequency detuning between the atoms, potentially leading to the failure of entanglement generation. By applying an intricate phase-space analysis of the I-CJC model, we demonstrate that a specific range of detunings allows for reliable entanglement generation across various initial conditions. Furthermore, we provide a means to quantify the relationship between the required minimum detuning and the phase of the field within the cavity. Notably, our research finds that as the phase of the field approaches zero, the required minimum detuning approaches zero, allowing for the generation of a particular maximally entangled state independent of the exact value of the detuning.

Social media monitoring through sentiment analysis on platforms like Twitter enables
the creation of real-time illustrations that show how feelings towards certain topics
or individuals are distributed globally. This research develops a method for assessing
the emotional content of Twitter messages and creates an LSTM-based classification
model for this purpose. The proposed approach achieves superior performance in
comparison to existing evaluation results on a well-known dataset. Furthermore, this
study enhances the initial neural framework by incorporating a neural averaging
mechanism, leading to improved twitter sentiment classification performance. The
findings of this research are intended to facilitate sentiment analysis on various
social media platforms, enabling the real-time assessment of public sentiment towards
specific issues or figures, as well as generating associated visualizations.

A novel approach based on the shade radius concept is applied to analyze the thermodynamic behavior of non-linear charged AdS black holes. A shadow temperature is determined using the shade radius and general shadow temperature follows the law of corresponding states in a specific context. This approach is expressed using an universal equation of state (UEOS) derived from the equation of state (UEOS) for non-relativistic van der Waals (N-R VW) black holes in an RAdS context. This approach is confirmed graphically and analytically, showing that black holes with the same shade radius, shadow temperature, and charged parameter exhibit identical thermodynamic behavior.

Reconstructing a quantum state from tomograms is distinct from traditional methods like density matrix or Wigner function approaches. Unlike these approaches, state reconstruction from tomograms involves two additional steps: calibrating the tomogram and then determining the state from the calibrated data. This paper presents several examples of how a lack of quantum entanglement and the emergence of quantum entropy can cause a breakdown in a state's ability to synchronize across two independent subsystems, using continuous variables for a two-mode field as the primary illustration. Additionally, we use experimental data from a squeezed beam to demonstrate how density matrices can be inferred from two-dimensional (or multi-dimensional) tomograms.

Viewers of immersive videos can choose how deeply they want to engage with the content. Passive viewing, where a first-person perspective is implied, is one level of engagement. However, if key information like viewer height, posture, and demographic details could be determined, a more interactive and personalized experience would be possible. This research focuses on extracting viewer perspective information from immersive videos by training a new subtype of perspective prediction model using a new dataset, whose videos have corresponding subtitles describing the scene. We demonstrate the benefits of using natural language from subtitles to improve perspective prediction accuracy. This engagement would enable a range of automated functions, including automatic rotation to a level where the viewer is likely standing, cropping to a level where the viewer would see the most, and levelation to a straight-horizon view.

We enhance the efficiency of tensor network algorithms for handling thermal properties and dynamic behavior in one-dimensional critical systems. By incorporating a specific type of local precision variation into the isometry tensors within a Thermofield Double Tensor Network, we achieve first-order precision control across a broad frequency or temperature spectrum with significantly reduced computational effort. This method allows us to obtain precise thermal correlation data and spectral functions in real and momentum space, as well as for dynamic Gaudin models, by utilizing an optimized basis that minimizes computational time.

We develop a decoupling theory for a broad spectrum of short-rank random
measures, characterized by their behavior under the expectation of a specific
function multiplied with these measures. The core of our theory involves creating
a "decoupling constant" that reflects the maximum disparity between this function's
average value and its corresponding value when generated by an independent
copy. We express this constant in terms of a "restricted efficacy" that measures
the impact of these measures on the function's value. The decoupling constant
is then approximated through a combination of two components that reflect the
measures' scope of influence when limited to a certain set of favorable outcomes.
We demonstrate the application of this theory to a diverse group of measures,
such as those related to the Poisson process, the Cox process, and various
short-range random measures, yielding results that provide an improvement or a
novel approach to existing decoupling estimates.

The critical role of the $\mathcal{O}(s_{N} )$ contribution from infrared renormalons in the scalar non-singlet TMD PDF, based on a color dipole, is highlighted. A method is proposed to correct the leading non-singlet TMD PDF to include this correction. The correction's coefficient is calculated to be approximately $-0.311$. A similar correction can be applied to the singlet TMD PDF. The impact of this correction is compared to other corrections in the critical region of the small-$x$ Bjorken $x$ scale.

We describe a unique lattice structure consisting of a two-dimensional metallic pattern that reacts differently to opposite directions of circular polarization, enabling it to distinguish between them. By combining this lattice with a magnetic substance and eliminating its symmetries in a strategic way, we demonstrate its ability to differentiate between two opposite directions of circular polarization. We further explain how this lattice structure can be utilized to create a novel device that is sensitive to the direction of its environment, and we provide the corresponding mathematical and physical equations to describe its behavior and properties.

Decision trees are widely used in various applications due to their effectiveness and ease of interpretation. However, optimizing decision trees is an NP-hard problem, particularly when considering the common constraint of limiting the total number of nodes. We introduce a decision tree model that leverages the knowledge gained from arbitrary black-box models, enabling our approach to produce accurate models that outperform existing optimization methods on the popular UCI dataset collection. We test our method on nine different datasets and in a zero-shot setting on four unseen datasets, demonstrating the robustness of our decision tree approach that incorporates black-box knowledge. Additionally, we show that our approach can be effectively used in a few-shot setting for unseen data.

We have analyzed $3.0\,{\rm nb}^{-1}$ of $\bar{B}^0_s$ decays within the range $\bar{B}^0_s\to D^0\bar{D}^0$ within a specific mass range. During this study, we have measured the ratio of $\bar{B}^0_s\to D^0\bar{D}^0$ to $\,B^0_s\to D^0\bar{D}^0$ decays to be $(6.40\pm0.23\pm0.18)\%\,.` This measurement is consistent with the theoretical expectation from perturbative QCD calculations. We have also observed $B^0_s\to D^{*0}\bar{D}^0 K^0_S$ decays for the first time and measured a branching fraction of $(0.84\pm0.23\pm0.10)\,{\rm ps}^{-1}\,.` In addition, we have obtained upper limits for $B^0_s\to D^{*+}D^0\bar{K}^0_S$ and $B^0_s\to D^{*+} D^{*+}\bar{K}^0_S$ decays.

In significant advancements since 2004, diverse researchers discovered lattice-building methods from specific data about submodule relationships, including a new approach by Stanley using poset characteristics, and new methods by Herzog et al., with one based on poset properties and another, combinatorial, lattice construction method from partial submodule information.

In this work, we address the challenge of learning a task through observation when an agent must cooperate with another who is trying to cooperate with it. Unlike typical single-imitation learning scenarios, our setting involves a complex process where the second agent must first identify and interpret the intentions of the intermediary, and only then decide whether to imitate what it has seen. We develop a new framework known as Co-Imitation Learning to capture this three-step process of thinking, acting, and imitating. To further analyze this problem, we create the Chain-of-Thought dataset, consisting of 3,000 examples that incorporate text-based reasoning, and we propose a Chain-of-Imitation framework that enables the second agent to automatically carry out its role in this cooperative environment.

This paper provides a metric framework for codes, expanding on the concepts of distance and similarity. It offers a detailed discussion of PAC codes and contrasts them with other code categories. Additionally, the paper presents an efficient method for calculating the distance between pairs of PAC code symbols using the Watson and Crick distance, which can be particularly beneficial for large-scale implementations. We also present initial experiments on the performance of PAC codes.

Neural machine translation (NMT) models typically generate translations sequentially, where each word is dependent on the previous ones, an process that is slow and inefficient. In this work, we propose an method that generates entire translations at once, leveraging reinforcement learning (IRL) to improve the quality of translations produced by the NMT model. We evaluate this approach using a reinforcement learning algorithm that maximizes the likelihood of the agent receiving more reward, by generating high-quality translations. By fine-tuning the NMT model with this inverse reinforcement learning method, we observe that it consistently outperforms traditional fine-tuning strategies.

The study of open, driven quantum systems is highly compelling due to the non-trivial, often equilibrium-like steady states that result from periodic driving. In this study, we investigate the non-trivial features of time-averaged current and population fluctuations in a single two-level system under a lambda configuration, as they arise from the interplay of the driven system and its environment. Using an exact analytical approach, we derive the full, time-resolved asymptotic behavior of these systems in the long-time limit. The resulting expression, which is stable under small driving periods, holds for any level of driving intensity, drive frequency, and coupling to the environment. The derived expression matches the experimental and numerical data, facilitating a detailed understanding of the system's dynamics.

A submanifold within a Riemannian ambient space is said to have a biharmonic property if it represents a stationary submanifold under a bienergy functional under appropriate variations. A recurrent structure consists of a manifold M^n embedded in a Euclidean space EN with a function $\alpha$ and a tensor field $\rho$ of type (1,1). This paper classifies submanifoles with a recurrent biharmonic structure where the second fundamental form is orthogonal and the tensor field satisfies specific conditions.

A set of rational numbers is considered p/q-identifiable if a specific type of infinite word can be constructed such that the set of words it generates with denominators q equals the given set, where the denominator is the smallest possible for each corresponding numerator. This concept is generalized from previous work where a (q)-identifiable set is defined with a word that creates q-power minimal denominators for each word it generates. Similar to standard id-entropy, we define p/q-id-entropy and theic-entropy as extensions of id-entropy, and these entropies are related through inequality. Also, like traditional ideals, p/q-identifiable sets have properties of being closed under union and intersection, and we define the p/q-Krull ideal as the set of words whose q-denominators are q-power-identifiable.

MongoDB is a widely used, document-oriented database that facilitates application development. It has recently incorporated traditional transaction support with multi-document coherence. Our transaction coherence specification outlines how MongoDB manages the transactions that it processes. Our formalization is processed by Coq, a functional programming and verification tool, confirming the correctness of existing transactions as well as preventing potential bugs like those recently discovered and fixed in the system.

We demonstrate the $e$-positivity of chromatic symmetric functions for a specific
class of graphs known as trees with at most four distinct edge colors, which we
fully characterize, and also provide the $e$-positivity of these functions for
graphs limited to three colors. Moreover, an result by Postnikov is extended to
show that certain lower triangular matrices, derived from chromatic symmetric
functions, are inverse to one another.

Research on intricate networks has recently regained interest due to its relevance in various real-world scenarios, such as spin glasses, biological species interactions, and neurological disorders. Our work focuses on a hidden aspect of these networks by exploring spin reversal dynamics in a specific assembly of nanoscale triangular and diagonal structures. In this model, triangular bonds are represented by a triple connection between three nodes, while the remaining edges between node pairs are denoted as pairwise interactions. As the probability of these pairwise interactions changes, the overall network complexity shifts from being based on triangular connections to pairwise interactions, which may influence the reversal time of spins and their distribution patterns. Our findings highlight the influence of network geometry, specifically triangular and pairwise interactions, on reversal time distributions, and suggest the use of a novel statistical model – the composite TRP distribution – to better understand and describe these patterns.

The exact mechanisms driving the solar system's interstellar environment are driven by the solar wind, but the specific conditions of this wind near the inner solar system are still largely unknown. A new study aims to fill this knowledge gap by analyzing data from the Parker Solar Probe (PSP), a mission designed to travel through the interstellar environment after its initial four years of operation. The first analysis of PSP data from the Solar and Interplanetary Explorer (SISE) experiment focuses on solar wind parameters near the spacecraft's approach to the Sun. The SISE flow rate calculation is based on a wide range of solar wind characteristics, including their speed, temperature, and density at distances between 0.26 to 2.30 astronomical units from the Sun. The analysis reveals that the average distance at which the PSP flew, the sunward distance, is characterized by an extremely high energy flux, with an estimated range of 10^31 erg/s, and is around three times higher than previously recorded values from other space-based observatories. The analysis shows that energy flux values tend to be around three orders of magnitude greater than 10^28 erg/s as the orbits overlap, but can be up to 10 times greater as the unique PSP travels further out. The study also finds that the energy flux is correlated with past solar activity and varies significantly over time, with up to three orders of magnitude difference between the most and least intense conditions observed.
